answer:
In one randomized trial, 4:3 intermittent fasting led to greater weight loss than daily calorie restriction by about 6 pounds after one year [1]. That study involved 165 people and was published in the May 20, 2025, issue of Annals of Internal Medicine [1].

Another report on an April 2025 Annals trial found 4:3 fasting outperformed daily calorie restriction by 2.89 kg, a statistically significant difference [3]. In that trial, the fasting group lost 7.6 percent of body weight versus 5.0 percent in the daily-restriction group [3]. More than half of fasting participants (58%) lost at least 5 percent of body weight, compared with 47 percent on daily restriction [3].

However, a 2026 trial in Clinical Nutrition of more than 200 adults with obesity found that time-restricted eating “was not more beneficial with regard to reduction in body weight than daily calorie restriction” [2]. In that trial, the calorie-restriction-only group lost 6.3 kg, and the 1.8 kg difference was not statistically significant [2]. The authors concluded that intermittent fasting and continuous calorie restriction produce comparable weight loss when calories are matched [2]. A review cited by Medical News Today also concluded that intermittent fasting diets have similar benefits to continuous energy restriction for weight loss [4].
